headline: MERIDIAN MINING MNO SANTA HELENA BRAZIL: STACKED VMS DISCOVERY — 11.3m AT 0.8 g/t AU, 3.4% ZN, 0.2% CU BELOW KNOWN SYSTEM
source_name: Investing News Network / Meridian Mining plc (LSE: MNO)
snippet: Meridian Mining plc (LSE: MNO) reported August 11, 2026 assay results from drill hole CD-878 at the Santa Helena VMS project in Brazil, returning 11.3 metres at 0.8 g/t gold, 0.2% copper, 17.6 g/t silver, 3.4% zinc, and 0.6% lead from 199.8 metres depth — confirming stacked VMS mineralisation layers below the known system, with a second lower copper-rich layer returning 1.7 metres at 0.9% copper. Peak assays in the interval reached 7.31 g/t gold and 71.7 g/t silver, with visible gold observed in the core. All VMS layers remain open in multiple directions. Simultaneous reconnaissance drilling has commenced at the Jauru and Araputanga licence portfolio within the broader Mato Grosso project area. Stacked VMS discoveries are significant because each additional layer multiplies the potential resource tonnage without requiring lateral footprint expansion — the same geological architecture that defines major VMS camps like Flin Flon, Matagami, and the Iberian Pyrite Belt.

headline: AMAROQ AMAL NANOQ SOUTH GREENLAND: 2026 RESOURCE DRILLING LAUNCHED — THREE RIGS ON CENTRAL ZONE, MAIDEN RESOURCE TARGETED H2 2026
snippet: Amaroq Ltd. (LSE: AMAL) announced August 11, 2026 that three company-owned diamond drill rigs have been deployed to the Central Zone of its 100%-owned Nanoq Gold Project on the Nanortalik Gold Belt in South Greenland, with the 2026 program focused on increasing data density and testing lateral and depth continuity across the Central Zone before stepping out to West 1 and parallel targets. A maiden Mineral Resource Estimate is targeted for H2 2026. Infrastructure reconnaissance for a potential harbour/coastal landing facility and access road is also underway to support future development planning. Located 130 kilometres northeast of Amaroq's producing Nalunaq Gold Mine, Nanoq's 2025 discovery drilling returned high-grade intercepts including 187.4 g/t gold over 1.5 metres and 19.6 g/t gold over 4.9 metres in the Central Zone. Three rigs simultaneously drilling a single zone — rather than a phased approach — signals management is prioritising the speed of maiden resource delivery, consistent with a company that already has production experience at Nalunaq and is building a district-scale position in South Greenland.

headline: LARAMIDE LAM $5M STRATEGIC INVESTOR PLACEMENT AT $0.60 — URANIUM DEVELOPER FUNDS US AND AUSTRALIA PROJECT ADVANCE
snippet: Laramide Resources Ltd. (TSX: LAM) announced August 11, 2026 a non-brokered private placement of 8,350,000 common shares at $0.60 per share with a named strategic investor, raising gross proceeds of $5,010,000. Proceeds will fund the advancement of Laramide's uranium projects in the United States and Australia. A strategic investor placement — rather than a brokered financing — at a defined price signals a single sophisticated counterparty with an alignment thesis beyond passive capital; in the uranium sector, strategic placements at current uranium prices above $86/lb typically reflect confidence in project-specific timelines or portfolio positioning by a uranium-focused institution. Laramide's US and Australian project portfolio positions it across two of the jurisdictions most actively supported by Western government domestic uranium supply initiatives under the post-2025 China export control environment.

headline: LITHIUM ARGENTINA LAR Q2 2026: $141M FCF AT CAUCHARI-OLAROZ — 9,280 TONNES LCE AT DESIGN CAPACITY, NET DEBT SLASHED $114M
snippet: Lithium Argentina AG (TSX: LAR) reported Q2 2026 results on August 11, with the Cauchari-Olaroz brine operation generating over $141 million in free cash flow at the project level during the quarter — a milestone reflecting the asset reaching near-design-capacity production of 9,280 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. LAR's share of income from Cauchari-Olaroz was $12.3 million versus a share of loss of $0.4 million in Q2 2025, converting the group to net income of $1.3 million versus a net loss of $4.1 million year-on-year. Net debt was reduced by $114 million, with new debt facilities secured at under 5% interest — a significant refinancing achievement. An additional $27 million distribution was paid to LAR post-quarter, with further distributions expected in H2 2026 as an optimisation and debottlenecking program advances production efficiency above nameplate capacity. For lithium investors navigating a sector where many development-stage projects remain years from cash flow, Cauchari-Olaroz's ramp to design capacity at current lithium prices provides a rare operating proof point in the Jujuy brine district.
